clue.text: Difficult retreating in rich silk city

indicators.note: retreating says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone withdrawing into a wealthy city famous for silk, finding things hard going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' says the letters are tucked inside 'rich silk city'; 'retreating' says to read them right to left.
explanation.definitionFit: A ticklish situation is a delicate, awkward one, so the word serves as a synonym for tricky.

clue.text: Money kidnapper demands after time that's found in ship

indicators.note: after places the kidnapper's money following the letter for time

parts.note: a ransom is the money demanded for a hostage

explanation.surface: A kidnapper demands payment after a time aboard a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A transom is a crossbeam forming the flat stern of a boat, so it is part of a vessel.

parts.note: a char, short for charwoman, is a British cleaning lady

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A cleaner who is careful but in the end rushed off her feet.
explanation.definitionFit: Chary means wary or reluctant to take risks, a synonym of careful.

clue.text: Selects deal organised for tourist attraction

indicators.note: organised means the letters of these words are set out in a new order

explanation.surface: A travel agent picks out a package arranged for sightseers.
explanation.walkthrough: Leeds Castle is a medieval castle in Kent, England (not near the city of Leeds), visited by many tourists.
explanation.definitionFit: The Kent castle is a popular visitor site, an example of a place people tour.

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means the pieces are turned upside down, read bottom to top

parts.note: ma is mother
alas is an exclamation meaning unfortunately

explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns MA + ALAS over to give AM and SALA in reverse order.
explanation.definitionFit: A salaam is a respectful bow of greeting in Muslim and Indian tradition.

indicators.note: in speech says the word is to be heard spoken rather than read

parts.note: to give instruction is to teach, past tense taught

explanation.surface: A nervous teacher, strained while delivering a lesson out loud.
explanation.definitionFit: Tense and taut both describe something stretched tight, such as a rope or nerves; plain synonyms.

parts.note: as means like, in the manner of

indicators.note: opening points to the first letter of the word idiot's

parts.note: nine is a number, a figure

explanation.definitionFit: Asinine means donkey-like in foolishness, a synonym of silly.

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, so the first piece holds the second as a pen holds animals

explanation.walkthrough: 'penning' suggests writing, but it means enclosing here.
explanation.definitionFit: A tweet is a short post on the social network X, formerly Twitter, a type of short message.

clue.text: No longer asleep — needing a wash?

parts.note: the wash of a ship is the disturbed water it leaves behind, its wake

explanation.surface: Someone just out of bed and in need of a good scrub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wash' looks like soap and water but is the trail of water behind a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has stopped sleeping is conscious and up, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Policy to retain age of certain popes

indicators.note: to retain means the first piece holds the second within it

parts.note: a policy is a party line
an eon is an age

explanation.surface: Church policy kept unchanged for an era of the papacy.
explanation.walkthrough: Leonine is usually 'lion-like', but it also means relating to a pope called Leo.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective refers to any of the pontiffs named Leo, so it describes certain popes.

parts.note: reads as 'mistaken from the outset' but means the very first wrongdoing, Adam and Eve's in Eden

explanation.surface: A complaint that something was mistaken from the beginning.
explanation.definitionFit: Christian doctrine holds that humankind inherits the first transgression, committed at the very beginning of history.

definitions.meaning: having a voice in a decision, as in 'have your ___'

explanation.surface: Free speech, illustrated with an instance.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun means a chance to voice an opinion, and the same word introduces an instance, as e.g. does.

indicators.note: upset means the letters of these words are knocked over and rearranged

explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' sounds like hurt feelings but signals rearranging the letters of ISN'T LAST I.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower of Stalin's brand of communism sits on the far left of politics.

parts.note: mi is the third note of the sol-fa scale
D is the abbreviation for duke, twice
ay is an old or dialect word for yes, indeed

explanation.walkthrough: 'twelve' stands for twelve o'clock, not the number of anything.

clue.text: Difference of opinion admitted by the German wanderer

parts.note: der is German for 'the'
a rift is a disagreement or split

explanation.surface: A German confesses to a disagreement with a traveller.
explanation.definitionFit: A drifter moves aimlessly from place to place, much like a rover.

definitions.meaning: the idiom 'not my ___' means not my concern or job
a common dove-like bird of towns

explanation.surface: Looking after a bird is one person's special duty.
explanation.definitionFit: The British idiom 'that's not my pigeon' means not my business; the word also names a familiar bird.

clue.text: Sisters here in turn, one early regularly

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of these words, starting with the second

explanation.surface: Nuns rising early here, one after another.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the 2nd, 4th, 6th letters and so on of IN TURN ONE EARLY.
explanation.definitionFit: A convent is where religious sisters live, so it is the place nuns are found.

clue.text: Charitable donations cut on old street? Very nearly

parts.note: alms are gifts to the poor

explanation.definitionFit: Almost and very nearly both mean not quite, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Extraordinarily call sit-in for small thing

indicators.note: extraordinarily means the letters are arranged out of their ordinary order

explanation.walkthrough: 'Extraordinarily' reads as an adverb of emphasis but tells you to rearrange CALL SIT-IN.
explanation.definitionFit: A scintilla is a tiny trace or spark, as in 'not a scintilla of evidence'.

clue.text: Sober and sedate way to help

parts.note: ST, street, is a way
aid is help

explanation.surface: Advice on a calm, sensible approach to helping others.
explanation.definitionFit: Staid describes someone serious, respectable and unexciting, matching both sober and sedate.

clue.text: With one's own enthusiastic Romeo, first of all — this one?

explanation.definitionFit: A suitor courting a beloved, as Romeo courts Juliet, is the person described.

indicators.note: fashioned means the letters are shaped into a new form

explanation.walkthrough: 'fashioned' fits the clothing picture, but it signals rearranging RED COAT.
explanation.definitionFit: The geometric decorative style flourished in the 1920s and 1930s, so the decade serves as a fair description.

definitions.meaning: the place near Perth where Scottish kings were crowned on the Stone of ___

explanation.surface: A tea cake sold at a historic Scottish site.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a small British teatime bake and the ancient crowning place of Scottish kings.
